intended_object: For a finite projective module M over a commutative ring R and a nonempty fiber of the locally constant stalk-rank function p ↦ rank_{R_p} M_p on Spec R, this is that fiber, the locus {p ∈ Spec R : rank M_p = n}, viewed as a clopen subset of Spec R. Inferred from the docstring and from how the module uses it (the idempotents in the rank-fiber decomposition).
explanation:
The definition's underlying set is `i.1`. Here `i : Function.Fiber (rankLocallyConstant R M)` is the preimage `f⁻¹'{n}` of the stalk-rank function `rankAtStalk M` for some value n that the function actually takes. The proof that this set is clopen rewrites `i.1` as `f⁻¹'{i.image}` and then uses `IsLocallyConstant.isClopen_fiber`. So the definition really is the rank-n locus, packaged as a `Clopens`, which matches the docstring.

The hypotheses are the standard ones. `Module.Finite` and `Module.Projective` are exactly what Mathlib's `isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk` needs (through finite presentation) to make the rank function locally constant. Nothing beyond these is assumed: there is no connectedness or nontriviality assumption, and the empty spectrum of the zero ring is covered (there are then no fibers).

Mathlib proves that fibers of locally constant functions are clopen. As far as I found, it has no definition bundling the rank-n locus of a projective module as a clopen set. A generic "fiber of a `LocallyConstant` function as a `Clopens`" would be a general topological helper. This definition is a specific instance of it for the rank function, and a specific object is not too narrow just because it is specific.
